# A Canadian company borrows US dollars twice, buys US shares with a broker
# charging its fee in US dollars, and sells part of the holding to repay. The
# share rises 60% and the US dollar falls from 1.40 to 1.10 and back to 1.20,
# so every figure has two movements in it.
#
# What happens:
#
# - 2028-01-02  20,000.00 CAD of opening capital.
# - 2028-01-05  1,000.00 USD borrowed at 1.30 — 1,300.00 CAD in the bank and
#               1,300.00 CAD of debt.
# - 2028-01-06  10 shares bought at 99.00 USD with a 1.00 USD broker charge,
#               991.00 USD in all, stated wholly in US dollars. The dollars
#               leave a cost basis carrying 1.30, so 1,288.30 CAD of cost goes
#               with them — and it is divided the way the dollars were:
#               990.00 USD to the shares at 1,287.00 CAD, which is 128.70 a
#               share, and 1.00 USD to the broker at 1.30 CAD. The 9.00 USD
#               left over stays in the bank at 1.30.
#
#               The broker fee expense account is kept in Canadian dollars,
#               because an expense is what it cost on the day it was incurred
#               and does not change afterwards. Kept in US dollars it would
#               hold 1.00 USD, and every statement drawn later would convert
#               that balance at its own rate.
# - 2028-06-30  1,010.00 USD borrowed at 1.10 to repay the first loan with
#               10.00 USD of interest. The debt cost 1,300.00 CAD and
#               1,000.00 USD now costs 1,100.00, so settling it realizes a
#               gain of 200.00 CAD.
# - 2028-12-30  7 shares sold at 158.40 USD, the 60% rise. They cost 900.90
#               CAD — 7 at 128.70 — and fetch 1,108.80 USD at the 1.20 of the
#               day, which is 1,330.56 CAD, so 429.66 CAD is realized on the
#               shares.
# - 2028-12-31  the second loan repaid with 1,030.00 USD, being 1,010.00 of
#               principal and 20.00 of interest. That debt cost 1,111.00 CAD
#               and 1,010.00 USD now costs 1,212.00, so settling it loses
#               101.00 CAD.
#
# What is left at the year end: 3 shares costing 386.10 CAD, 87.80 USD in the
# bank, and no debt.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_a_broker_fee_two_us_loans_and_part_of_the_shares_sold.py.

# Stated wholly in US dollars, which is how a US broker's confirmation reads.
# The 991.00 USD leave a cost basis carrying 1.30, and that rate travels with
# them: 990.00 USD of it onto the shares and 1.00 USD of it onto the fee.
2028-01-06 * "Buy 10 shares at 99.00 USD, broker 1.00 USD"
	currency.mnemonic: "USD"
	Assets:Shares 10.0000 USD_CORP
		guid: "a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a10003"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD_CORP"
		share_price: "99"
		value: "990.00"
	Expenses:Brokerage 1.30 CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		share_price: "10/13"
		value: "1.00"
	Assets:USD Bank -991.00 USD
		cost_basis_split_guid: "a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a10001"
